title: Send alerts through the channel config names

blocks.text: Every service sends its operational alerts through one channel, chosen in its config under `alerts.channel`: `email`, `sms`, `chat`, or whatever else the build provides. Services that don't set the key send by email. Last week a service was deployed with a misspelled channel name, and its disk-full alert was the first anyone heard of it, after the disk had filled.

Write `choose` in `src/main/java/practice/AlertService.java`. The constructor calls it once, and `raise` sends every alert through the channel it returns. A misspelled name must be found when the service is deployed, by an `IllegalArgumentException` from the constructor, and must never send an alert anywhere else. About five lines in total.

cases.says: every alert goes through the channel config names, and through no other
a channel name the build doesn't know makes the constructor throw IllegalArgumentException
a channel name the build doesn't know never sends an alert through another channel
when config names no channel, alerts go by email

origin.section: Resolve a Strategy's Name When the Service Starts, Not When It First Runs

concepts: A default belongs to a config key that is absent, never to a value that is wrong.
A strategy named in config is resolved when the service starts, and an unknown name makes start-up fail; a lookup at first use fails after the deploy, and a fallback for an unknown name never fails.
